questions.question: Does a pilot see their own running Bleed total, or is it GM-only?
questions.resolution: Resolved 2026-09-06, with a better answer than either option originally posed: Bleed is neither passively visible nor permanently hidden - it is TESTED. A pilot spends a discretionary slice on a Harmonics Evaluation to learn the current value, and that same evaluation can also improve it. Information becomes a purchase in personal time, matching the pattern contactPool.analysisDutyInteraction already set. See config.json bleed.visibilityMechanism and timeEconomy.options#harmonics-evaluation.
questions.notes: 2026-09-06 analysis (design/resonance-and-bleed.md §3) argues this one is not neutral: Pushing trades Resonance now for Bleed later, and a trade with one side hidden is a gamble rather than a decision. Recommended middle path — show the pilot a BAND (Stable/Strained/Critical) rather than a number: enough to price a push honestly, not enough to count down precisely to berserk, and it matches the three-light-gauge idiom the console already uses. Still open; a recommendation is not a decision.

questions.question: Does the Day 1 pilot get a genuine, viable option to sit out the second Contact? If yes, what does refusal actually cost — and is it survivable as a choice, or does the story punish it into a non-choice?
Is Frame class a psych-profile "verdict" the kid didn't choose, or player-selected? The verdict version is stronger characterisation but takes a build choice away from the player.
questions.notes: Asked directly and the answer given was about something bigger: Frame builds (class, equipment, even the mech itself) aren't fixed at creation at all — players can swap/upgrade over the whole campaign via an in-universe correspondence/negotiation system (see relatedRefs), balanced case by case. Still genuinely open whether the INITIAL assignment at creation is a verdict or player-chosen — that ongoing-negotiation answer doesn't resolve it either way.

questions.question: Are all six Resonance percentages read aloud and ranked at weekly harmonics testing (public, competitive, cruel), or kept private to each pilot?
questions.notes: 2026-09-06 analysis (design/resonance-and-bleed.md §2) leans hard toward public: published ranking turns Resonance from a character stat into a public score of how emotionally available a child is, assigned by an institution — the cruellest and strongest use of the mechanic. gm-notes.json read-numbers-flatly already points the same way. Still the user call.

questions.question: Keep the Transparency Advocate as written, reshape them, or cut back to a two-pole Commander/Caretaker structure?
Is at least one Frame's permanent loss a planned campaign beat, or left to emerge from play?
Do the other five know the pilot in scene 7 (Episode One) is one of their own, or do they just see a machine? Ignorance is more frightening; knowledge is more binding.
PCs with a visibly non-human ancestry present as outwardly human, revealing their true nature over time — what's the in-fiction reason this works, and how does it tie into ongoing campaign events?
questions.resolution: Anabala/Mitflit-adjacent: tied to whatever happened in the unfinished prior campaign — Anabala and/or the Mitflits know something concrete about it, making her a literal, in-fiction source of the answer rather than unexplained lore. The discovery vector is now locked too: character creation includes a mandatory DNA test as part of Civil Defence Force clearance, which flags 'irregularities' in affected PCs — hard to explain, not disqualifying (the character is still cleared for active duty). Exact mechanism (what actually happened, why the DNA reads irregular, and how Anabala/the Mitflits' knowledge connects to it) still to be worked out together — the direction and discovery vector are locked, the underlying explanation isn't.

questions.question: Is the school the same physical campus as "the huge facility" the kids report to for civil-defense/Frame shifts, or two separate locations? A combined campus is thematically appealing (institutionalized militarization of education) but not confirmed.
questions.resolution: Same combined campus — the militarization-of-education reading was confirmed as the intended one.

questions.question: What local ground forces exist for non-piloting students to command during a Contact, what can they be ordered to do, and how does that command interact with the mech-scale fight? Needs enough depth that leaning into ground command is as satisfying a whole-campaign arc as piloting.

Working consecutive time-of-day segments without resting is confirmed (2026-09-06) to trigger a check that gets harder each additional segment worked, ending in involuntary unconsciousness and the loss of that segment's slot. The structure is settled; the numbers are not — what check (Fortitude is the likely fit, not confirmed), what's the starting DC and the per-segment escalation, and does it reset fully on any rest or only on specific rest types?
questions.notes: Closely linked to rest-activity-roster — the reset mechanism likely depends on which rest types end up designed. A concrete proposal exists (2026-09-06, design/downtime-activities.md §1): a four-stage Exhaustion track built from real conditions (Fatigued → +Slowed 1 → +Stupefied 1 → Unconscious), and Fortitude DC 15 escalating by 5 per consecutive segment. Not confirmed — a researched suggestion, not a decision.

questions.question: Confirmed (2026-09-06) that resting is a real, encouraged, multi-typed choice with different SF2E-relevant bonuses per type — a quiet option weighted toward HP recovery, hospital care targeting HP and debuffs, a social outing (clubbing/karaoke) for a different kind of bonus, and more. The structure is settled; the actual roster of named rest activities and their specific mechanical bonuses is explicitly future collaborative design, not something to invent to look complete.
questions.notes: Closely linked to fatigue-escalation-formula. A concrete proposal exists (2026-09-06, design/downtime-activities.md §2): Lights Out (Long-Term Rest's real doubled HP recovery), Sick Bay (real Treat Wounds numbers), Night Out (−1 Bleed + a circumstance bonus, since Bleed's own sources already include psychological distress), plus Workshop offered as a fourth illustrative option. Not confirmed — a researched suggestion, not a decision.

questions.question: Bleed is 0-10 with a single threshold at 10 (berserk), so points 1-9 currently have no mechanical expression at all — a tracked resource that stays invisible in play until it detonates. Should Bleed gain intermediate thresholds, and should they eat what Resonance grants (e.g. 4+ costs your reaction, 7+ drops your effective band one step for ability access) so the two tracks actually interact before the endpoint?
questions.notes: Flagged 2026-09-06 as the highest-value, lowest-cost change available on either track. Also makes Pushing a genuinely tense trade: a band now for a band later.

questions.question: Bleed has four defined sources (pushing, Frame damage, plug distress, Suppression) and exactly one undefined reduction (Signals Liaison reduces Bleed, no magnitude or rate given). With no decay, no per-session reset and no downtime route, berserk arrives on a schedule regardless of player choices — a countdown rather than a managed risk. Is that the intent? If not, what are Bleed sinks and at what rates?
questions.notes: A one-way doom clock is a legitimate structure (Blades in the Dark, Ten Candles) but it changes the interesting decision from avoiding berserk to choosing when it lands, which only works if Bleed is visible (see bleed-visibility). Episode 1 scripts berserk into the very first fight, which suggests the countdown reading may already be the de facto intent. design/downtime-activities.md proposes one sink (Night Out, -1).

questions.question: config.json bandDesignNote states that most of the campaign is played at 2 actions. SF2E is architecturally a three-action system — two-action activities consume a whole turn, the signature turn shapes need three, and the multiple attack penalty is built around a third attack being possible-but-unwise. Should 3 actions instead be the norm from Nominal upward, with 2 reserved for Dead Weight as a genuine failure state, letting ability tiers and internal-power duration carry the band spread?
questions.resolution: Resolved 2026-09-06: 3 actions is the norm from Nominal upward; 2 actions is a penalty state with exactly two causes, Dead Weight sync and Frame damage (Degraded caps at 2, Critical at 1). User's framing: 'we need to build around the normal being 3 actions and 2 actions being the penalty for early campaign usage and for usage when the mech is seriously damaged.' config.json updated; reasoning preserved in resonance.actionEconomyRevisionNote.
questions.notes: Raised 2026-09-06. The counter-argument is real and artistic: constraint IS the fiction, and Harmonised should feel like a breakthrough. The concern is that a reduced action economy delivers both feels-constrained and has-fewer-decisions, and only the first is wanted.

questions.question: Measured total combat contribution across the Resonance bands (actions per round x internal-power rounds, plus Absolute free Strikes) is 7 / 12 / 24 / 40 actions — a 5.7x spread from Dead Weight to Absolute, before ability tiers are counted. That is a wider gap than four character levels in SF2E, on one track, inside one tier, between players at the same table. Is that intended, and if so should pilots fielded together be constrained to within a band or two of each other?
questions.resolution: Addressed 2026-09-06 by the action-economy change rather than by capping who deploys together. With 3 actions from Nominal, the normal operating range (Nominal to Absolute) compresses from 3.3x to 2.2x. Dead Weight to Absolute remains 5.7x, which is now correct rather than alarming: Dead Weight is explicitly the failure state, and a pilot below 40% sync being a fraction of a working Frame is the intended fiction. The original concern was pilots at 55% being in that position, which no longer happens.
questions.notes: Arithmetic run 2026-09-06; it had not been computed before. Closely tied to two-action-default — making 3 actions standard from Nominal compresses the action-count spread to roughly 2.2x and shifts the difference onto ability tiers, which is arguably where it belongs anyway.

questions.question: Suppression currently triggers when a player declines an Anchor-relevant conflict specifically to protect their deployability — which requires the GM to judge a player motive and then penalise them for it. Should it instead trigger on pattern (a kid Anchors going untouched for N scenes raises Bleed regardless of why), keeping the same anti-exploit pressure without anyone at the table having to assess intent?
questions.notes: Raised 2026-09-06. The current version also risks penalising a legitimate characterisation — some kids genuinely are conflict-avoidant.

questions.question: SF2E Hero Points can be spent to avert death. Berserk (Bleed 10) currently has no escape valve at all. Should spending all Hero Points be able to avert or interrupt berserk the way it averts death, giving loss-of-self the same mechanical dignity as death and handing players one expensive out?
questions.notes: Raised 2026-09-06. Also worth being deliberate about the broader overlap: Hero Points and Anchors both reward selfless or daring play and will often fire on the same moments, at different timescales.

questions.question: Frames DO level up (confirmed 2026-09-06; campaign-arc.md had already corrected the design bible on this). The new model: players earn upgrade points from downtime activities AND from winning both personnel- and Frame-scale combat, spend them on Frame upgrades, and enough points levels the Frame — a normal SF2E level-up with bespoke Frame feats and options. Combat awards guarantee a floor so no Frame is ever stranded at 12. Open parameters: what are the points called, what is the points-to-level conversion, are they per-pilot or drawn from a shared pool like technician-days, and what are the concrete DOWNSIDES of over-investing in Frame upgrades at the expense of personal activities?
questions.notes: PARTIALLY ANSWERED 2026-09-06. (a) DRIFT: hard cap of one level either way. User: 'rewards players up to a point for investment but doesn't allow there to be an overpowering advantage to just doing frame stuff', and it keeps the encounter maths reliable. This supersedes campaign-arc.md's strict-lockstep line, which is now annotated there. (b) POOL: upgrade points are INDIVIDUAL per pilot, not shared like technician-days — each PC has their own repair crew (see repair-crew-relationship). STILL OPEN: what the points are called, and the points-to-level conversion rate.

questions.question: Downtime activities grant flavoured, predictable buffs — the user's example: 'they only have to go to the gun range once to get a buff which they know will make their next personnel level battle easier by making it easier to hit baddies.' DURATION ANSWERED 2026-09-06: a buff persists until used, and is spent on the character's next combat — bankable, one-shot, not use-it-or-lose-it. STILL OPEN: whether several different buffs can be carried into the same fight, and whether there is a cap.
questions.notes: Useful half-answer already in the system: if activity buffs are expressed as CIRCUMSTANCE bonuses, SF2E's own stacking rules cap them for free — two circumstance bonuses to the same roll don't stack, you take the highest, so hoarding three gun-range visits does nothing. Different bonus TYPES (circumstance + status + item) would all still apply, which is a natural, system-native ceiling rather than an invented one. The remaining risk to watch is a player banking several DIFFERENT-typed buffs ahead of a Contact they can see coming. The design principle is settled even though the parameters are not: buffs must be LEGIBLE and PLANNABLE — a player should be able to predict the payoff before spending the slice. That is the positive twin of ux-doctrine Law 19 (nothing expires without its cost being visible first). Circumstance bonuses are the safest vehicle since they are bounded and native to SF2E, and per design-layers.md this is a Layer 2 addition that must not distort the Layer 0 combat maths underneath.

questions.question: Each pilot has their own repair crew (confirmed 2026-09-06, alongside the decision that upgrade points are individual rather than pooled). The crew is a standing NPC relationship with real mechanical weight in both directions: treat them well — the user's example is going out drinking with them — and they may put in an unasked-for night shift; neglect them and they provide less HP healing per repair. Open parameters: how is crew standing tracked, what exactly does it scale (HP restored per technician-day? chance of free work? both?), how many named crew NPCs per pilot, and how does crew standing interact with the SHARED technician-day pool?
questions.notes: The two resources are cleanly non-redundant and should stay that way: the technician-day pool is the Directorate's SHARED allocation — how much repair time you are granted, competed for between pilots — while crew standing is PERSONAL and scales how much you get OUT of that time. Allocation vs effectiveness, two different axes. This also gives the Night Out rest activity (design/downtime-activities.md §2) a second payoff beyond Bleed reduction, and gives every pilot a recurring named NPC relationship that is professional rather than personal, sitting alongside Anchors rather than duplicating them. TERMINOLOGY WARNING: the user said 'ground crews' in passing, but these are NPC repair technicians and must stay verbally distinct from the PC-played Ground Roles in campaign/ground-roles.json (Sensor Operator, Umbilical Control, etc.), which are something else entirely.

questions.question: When one player learns a Character Card Fact about an NPC (design/npc-social-intel.md), does it become known to the whole party from then on, or only to the player/character who earned it? Proposed default: party-wide, matching how the muster board already treats party knowledge as one shared flag and how the Sensor Operator ground role already frames a discovered fact as something 'the pilot can act on' regardless of who found it.
questions.notes: Raised 2026-09-06. Changes whether 'who was actually in the room' ever matters for what the table can act on.

questions.question: design/npc-social-intel.md proposes a +2 circumstance bonus when a player's stated approach clearly uses a revealed Fact against an NPC. Is +2 the right size, matching the existing Night Out rest bonus, or should it scale with how directly the Fact applies?
questions.notes: Raised 2026-09-06. Low-stakes to leave open — easy to tune at the table without touching the surrounding design.

questions.question: Should an NPC's current Attitude (Hostile/Unfriendly/Indifferent/Friendly/Helpful, on the Character Card) ever be shown to players as the literal word, or only narrated through how the GM plays the scene? design/npc-social-intel.md proposes narrated-only by default.
questions.notes: Raised 2026-09-06. Distinct from bleed-visibility's resolution (tested, on request) — Attitude changes far more often and from many small actions, so a testing model may not fit as cleanly; open rather than assumed.
